title: Radio La Cosa Exacta: La puerta no vio nada

lines.text: COLD OPEN. A bus kneels at a curb. A zipper catches. At the end of an old corridor, a latch taps twice in the wind.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: On the radio you can see everything. That's the first lie I told myself when I took this job.

lines.speaker: JAIME
lines.text: (over intercom) The first lie was that you knew how to operate the espresso machine.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: I know how to operate it. I refuse to negotiate with its values.
THEME: three notes from a muted trumpet. A telephone line clicks.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: Good evening, neighbors. This is Radio La Cosa Exacta, where we ask what happened before announcing what we wish had happened. Tonight: somebody has sent us a picture of an apartment door, and somehow the whole building believes it proves a crime. Our producer Jaime has put the photograph in an envelope so I can't embellish it with my eyebrows.

lines.speaker: JAIME
lines.text: Your eyebrows have never accepted a chain of custody.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: We are not a courtroom, Jaime. That is exactly why we must be careful. First call—Antonia, you're on.

lines.speaker: ANTONIA
lines.text: Mi vecina me dijo que vio la puerta abierta a las diez. That's what I said. But the neighborhood message says I saw a stranger forcing it.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: What did you actually see?

lines.speaker: ANTONIA
lines.text: La foto. On my niece's phone. The door was closed in the photo, anyway. My neighbor said she saw it open earlier. I was buying bread.

lines.speaker: JAIME
lines.text: For the record, the bread was innocent.

lines.speaker: ANTONIA
lines.text: No lo sé. It was very expensive.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: We have three separate things: what the neighbor reported, what Antonia saw in the picture, and what someone imagined between them. Which one of those does the chat remember?

lines.speaker: ANTONIA
lines.text: The imagined one. It has better punctuation.
The studio door opens. A quiet woman in a raincoat enters without making eye contact with the microphone.

lines.speaker: MERCEDES
lines.text: I'm the building's evening caretaker. I heard you're describing our door.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: You can choose not to come on the air.

lines.speaker: MERCEDES
lines.text: I know. But I want to tell my side before the door acquires an attorney. I was closing the upper window when the wind pushed the latch. The door was open for perhaps twenty seconds. Nobody was forcing it.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: Are you certain about the twenty seconds?

lines.speaker: MERCEDES
lines.text: Approximately. I did not time it. The radio at the bakery was playing the chorus of something terrible.

lines.speaker: JAIME
lines.text: Please don't tell me it was our morning show.

lines.speaker: MERCEDES
lines.text: It was. The chorus was the weather forecast. Twice.
A second telephone line flashes. The tiny light in the booth looks like an impatient firefly.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: We also have an interpretation exercise, recorded by actors, that shows how a rumor can escape its owner. Let's hear the original witness account first.

lines.speaker: WITNESS ACTOR
lines.text: My neighbor told me that the door was open. I didn't see anyone enter.

lines.speaker: INTERPRETER ACTOR
lines.text: Mi vecina me dijo que la puerta estaba abierta. No vi entrar a nadie.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: That was the faithful version. Now listen to the fictional mistake.

lines.speaker: INTERPRETER ACTOR
lines.text: Vi a una persona entrar por la puerta abierta.
A bell sounds once, dry as a teaspoon striking a glass.

lines.speaker: ANTONIA
lines.text: ¡No! That's a completely different witness.

lines.speaker: JAIME
lines.text: In one sentence we've created a spectator, an entrant, and a certainty that weren't there.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: Exactly. The problem isn't the accent. It isn't whether the Spanish is elegant. It's that the speaker's limits were stolen. Can we repair it without turning the whole segment into a sermon?

lines.speaker: MERCEDES
lines.text: Play the original again. The people listening can do the work.
They do. This time the silence after the sentence is long enough to hear rain touch the studio window.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: Mercedes, what do you want the neighbors to know?

lines.speaker: MERCEDES
lines.text: That somebody should repair the latch, and somebody else should apologize to the woman they accused. I have more important gossip: the community garden has grown three tomatoes in October.

lines.speaker: ANTONIA
lines.text: Three? They said there were nine.

lines.speaker: JAIME
lines.text: Here we go again.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: (softening) We may have solved the door. We have not solved the internet. At least the tomatoes are still negotiable.
The photograph is finally removed from its envelope. It's a close-up of the latch, taken a week before the rumor. A penciled note on the back says, “Ask maintenance.”

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: That is our final fact for tonight: a photo can show a latch; it cannot show what somebody witnessed on another day.
THEME RETURNS, interrupted by Jaime's espresso machine grinding with the determination of a small construction vehicle.

lines.speaker: JAIME
lines.text: I got it to make coffee.

lines.speaker: NORA
lines.text: Is it coffee?

lines.speaker: JAIME
lines.text: I wouldn't testify to that.
END. The call-in line remains open for listeners who want to hear the two versions again.
